task: Write a 70–105-word close reading for a high-school literature notebook. Readers know the ordinary meanings of silence and quarter-hour but are learning how neighboring sentences can complicate a narrator's description. Use both original sentences exactly if quoting. Offer a defensible reading of the contrast, such as possible irony or exaggeration, without declaring a unique authorial intention or diagnosing the narrator. A focused paragraph is sufficient; no external critics or compulsory counterargument are needed.

facts.text: The complete supplied original excerpt is “Our street was perfectly silent. The bell rang every quarter-hour.”
Both sentences belong to the same narrator's description of the street.
The packet supplies no author commentary, further plot, or information about the narrator's health.

forbidden_additions: An invented author biography, later scene, or critical consensus
An assertion that the packet proves a single intended interpretation
preserve: The relationship between the two descriptions rather than an isolated keyword judgment
